messages:
oncall-bot: Paging: SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate — p95 latency spiked above 1200ms and p99 streaming stalls observed. Alert threshold crossed at 2024-11-03T14:22:47Z (ts 3951234567). Auto-paging to oncall.

alex (sre): acked — I'm on it. collecting context. Any immediate customer reports? :eyes:

rachel (deploy): @alex support-bot just created a ticket: several customers seeing streaming stalls/timeouts. I pushed a small template rendering change ~10m ago (deploy 3951234000). deploy-bot: Deployment 3951234000 by rachel completed 10m ago in prod.

olivia (eng-runtime): seeing huge tail in the preproc tier. Preproc pods CPU >90%, queue-depth on preproc service rising from 2->18, per-request preproc time p95 450ms -> 2.3s, p99 1.1s -> 6.2s. Tokenizer time component dominated. Logs show heavy JSON-mode template expansion + tool-schema rendering for large tool sets.

max (eng-ml): I can confirm traces showing many requests hit the new tool-schema renderer path that expands nested JSON output schema. That path does repeated tokenization for validation and example generation. A single request can force extra tokenization passes (2-4x). Combined with streaming, that amplifies tail latency.

alex (sre): any evidence it's a code regression vs traffic pattern? traffic looks normal except a few large customers sending tool-heavy prompts.

olivia (eng-runtime): it's a 2-factor: rollout of rachel's template change increased JSON-mode usage on some routes, and a spike from one partner sending long tool schemas. Before change JSON-mode was opt-in and mostly off. Now some routes flipped on. We are seeing prefix cache misses for JSON-mode so no KV cache hit.

rachel (deploy): I can rollback the template change immediately if that's the fastest fix. Standby for rollback approval.

carmen (product): what is customer impact? are any SLAs currently breached? which customers are affected? we need to triage customer comms.

support-bot: Tickets created: #5834 (AcmeCorp), #5835 (BrightHealth), #5836 (EduLabs). Two timeouts reported, three degraded streaming responses. All are on Dedicated / high-throughput routes.

alex (sre): mitigation plan (short): 1) disable JSON-mode feature-flag for streaming endpoints 2) route critical customers to fallback tokenizer pool that uses simpler tokenization (lower CPU) 3) scale preproc horizontally and increase pod CPU for short window 4) rollback rachel's template change if needed.

olivia (eng-runtime): I'm toggling feature-flag now (`/featureflag set streaming.json_mode false --env=prod --routes=/v1/streaming/*`). Expecting propagation in ~30s. Also warming fallback tokenizer pool.

olivia (eng-runtime): command output:
```
$ /featureflag set streaming.json_mode false --env=prod --routes=/v1/streaming/*
OK: flags updated (propagation start)
Propagation: 0% -> 100% (approx 45s)
```

alex (sre): scaling preproc:
```
kubectl scale deployment/preproc --replicas=18 -n prod
kubectl get hpa preproc -n prod
```
Scaling applied. Also applied an ingress rule to route 20% traffic to fallback-tokenizer pool.

deploy-bot: Rollback candidate ready: revert commit rachel/changeset/8721. Manual approval required.

rachel (deploy): I approve rollback. Rolling back now.

rachel (deploy): rollback complete (deploy 3951234701). Monitoring.

olivia (eng-runtime): after disabling JSON-mode and rolling back, preproc p95 dropped from ~2.3s -> 420ms within 2 minutes. p99 decreased from 6.2s -> 900ms. Streaming stall count reduced 10x. Queue-depth back to baseline.

support-bot: Customer ticket update: AcmeCorp confirmed improved responses, no longer timing out. BrightHealth still seeing rare stalls — investigating tail.

max (eng-ml): note: fallback tokenizer reduces validation and schema-expansion checks. It is safe for streaming but loosens some JSON-mode invariants. This is acceptable as a live mitigation but we need follow-up to avoid correctness regressions.

carmen (product): request: prepare customer-facing summary for affected customers and list of mitigations + ETA for permanent fix.

alex (sre): immediate incident status: SLOs restored for streaming endpoints. Root cause hypothesis: combined effect of template change (rolled out 10m prior) enabling JSON-mode paths + burst of tool-schema heavy payloads from partner -> exponential tokenizer work and cache misses -> preproc CPU saturation -> tail latency / streaming stalls. Next steps: short postmortem, customer outreach, and action items below.

olivia (eng-runtime): observed artifacts:
- repeated tokenization passes in traces under `preproc.render_schema()`
- cache keys inconsistent due to ephemeral example IDs, causing low prefix cache hit rate
- heavy CPU due to nested example generation loops

max (eng-ml): permanent mitigations suggested:
- precompile tool-schema templates offline and store compiled artifacts in cache
- add guardrails: reject tool-schema expansions above token threshold with 429+explain header
- JSON-mode: add streaming-optimized codepath that reuses KV cache and avoids full validation during streaming responses
- add alerting on preproc cache hit rate and per-customer tool-schema size

rachel (deploy): action items: revert promoted change (done), patch CI to run schema-expansion perf tests, add deployment gating metric for preproc latency.

alex (sre): action items for SRE/Oncall:
- run postmortem (owner: alex)
- contact top affected customers with timeline + root-cause (owner: carmen)
- add temporary rate-limits on large tool-schema routes (owner: alex/rachel)

olivia (eng-runtime): follow-up plan: 1) implement compiled schema artifacts and streaming-optimized JSON-mode (PR planned) 2) add prefix cache consistency fixes 3) run a canary with synthetic heavy-tool requests before flipping JSON-mode back on.

support-bot: marking incident resolved for now — monitoring for 1h. If p95/p99 regress, re-open thread.

alex (sre): closing notes: SLOs restored, live mitigations applied (feature-flag off, rollback, scale, routing). Postmortem within 48h. Great cross-team response. :raised_hands:

carmen (product): thanks all. I'll draft the customer note and approve it with legal. Expect outreach in next 6-8h.

olivia (eng-runtime): leaving follow-up tasks in the incident board: `INC-3951234567`.

support-bot: Incident status: RESOLVED -> Monitoring (since 3951235023).
